source_refs.note: Advantages of CT-Scan: a main subheading of 20.4 Computed Tomography Scanning (CT-Scan), its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 163-164.

blocks.text: CT scans offer several important advantages over traditional X-rays. While single X-ray images are still useful and quick to produce, they only give a flat, two-dimensional view. In contrast, CT scans produce three-dimensional images, allowing doctors to see the size, shape, and exact location of organs, bones, and other structures inside the body. This makes it easier to distinguish between tissues, even when they have very similar densities. For example, a CT scan can clearly show the position and size of a tumor, which helps doctors accurately target it during treatment using high-energy X-rays or gamma rays. However, it is important to remember that CT scans involve exposure to X-rays, which are a form of ionizing radiation. Although the amount of radiation is relatively low, it still carries a small risk to the patient. On average, the radiation dose from a CT scan is about one-third of the natural background radiation a person receives in a year, or roughly equal to the radiation dose received during four long-distance flights. Therefore, doctors take special precautions, especially when scanning pregnant women or patients with existing health concerns.

blocks.title: Tidbits
blocks.text: CT scanners take multiple X-ray images from different angles to reconstruct a 2D cross-section of the body. When these slices of the body are combined, they create a 3D model like stacking layers of a cake.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The book says a CT scan gives on average about one-third of a year's natural background radiation, or about four long-distance flights. Typical CT doses are much larger: about 2 mSv for the head (about 8 months of background radiation) to about 7-10 mSv for the chest or abdomen (about 2-3 years, with background at about 2.4-3 mSv per year). A long-haul flight gives only about 0.03-0.1 mSv, so the book's two comparisons also disagree with each other.
